program.help:
Identify and remove the EMG component of a multichannel extracellular .dat using FastICA, and write the EMG events out as if they were spikes.
C++ port of the algorithmic core of the labbox MATLAB EMG_removing toolbox (Chen 2019), restricted to the configuration the toolbox uses by default: deflation FastICA with the pow3 nonlinearity, run on high-pass filtered data, with the EMG component selected as the IC whose loading is most spatially uniform.
Inputs: <session>.dat <session>.{xml,yaml,yml} (acquisitionSystem and spikeDetection blocks read)
Outputs (per spikeDetection group, 1-based): <session>-emgclean.dat int16, same shape as .dat, EMG component subtracted <session>.emg.<g> int16 1-channel EMG_au trace (sample-rate-aligned) <session>.res.<g>.emg int64-LE event timestamps (sample indices) <session>.spk.<g>.emg int16 nSamples × nChannels per-event waveforms <session>.emg.meta.yaml sidecar: per-group loading, unmixing, threshold, FastICA diagnostics
Pipeline: 1. Pass 1 — read up to idDuration seconds starting at idStart, demean per channel, apply 4th-order Butterworth high-pass at hpFreq, downsample by `downsample`, run FastICA deflation pow3 with K = max(round(0.8·nch), min(16, nch)). EMG component = column k of A maximising |sum( A[:,k] / ||A[:,k]|| )|. Threshold = thresholdFactor · 1.4826 · MAD(|EMG_au|) on the un-filtered subsample. 2. Pass 2 — stream the full .dat in chunks of `chunkSamples` samples per channel. For each sample compute EMG_au[t] = (raw[t,:] − μ) · Ws, then write clean[t,c] = raw[t,c] − As[c]·EMG_au[t] to <session>-emgclean.dat and EMG_au itself to <session>.emg.<g>. 3. Event detection — smooth |EMG_au| with a boxcar of envelopeWindowMs, find threshold-crossings separated by ≥ refractoryPeriod, refine each peak inside a peakSearchLength window. 4. Pass 3 — for each event timestamp, mmap the original .dat and extract a (nSamples × nChannels(g)) int16 waveform window into <session>.spk.<g>.emg.
Run BEFORE ndm_hipass / ndm_extractspikes if you want spike detection to operate on the EMG-cleaned signal (use <session>-emgclean.dat as the source for downstream filtering — the wrapper does NOT rename .dat itself; renaming or symlinking is the operator's call). Run AFTER spike detection if you want the .res.<g>.emg / .spk.<g>.emg events purely for analysis without disturbing the spike-extraction pipeline.
# hpFreq
High-pass cutoff in Hz applied during FastICA component identification (default 100). EMG dominates frequencies above the LFP corner; raising this above the LFP band biases the leading IC towards the muscle component.
# thresholdFactor
Event-detection threshold expressed as a multiple of the robust noise estimate 1.4826 · MAD(|EMG_au|). Default 5.0 — increase to capture only large bursts; lower to capture more low-amplitude EMG.
# envelopeWindowMs
Length of the boxcar smoothing window applied to |EMG_au| before peak detection (milliseconds). Default 20. Roughly the burst-fusion timescale.
# refractoryPeriod
Minimum number of samples between consecutive accepted events. Default 0 → derive from envelopeWindowMs.
# peakSearchLength
Number of samples after a threshold crossing within which the local maximum is found. Default 0 → use refractoryPeriod.
# downsample
Subsampling factor applied to the high-pass filtered identification data before FastICA. Default 3. Larger values trade ID accuracy for memory + speed.
# idStart, idDuration
Time window in seconds (relative to the start of .dat) over which FastICA observes the data to identify the EMG component. Default 0 + 60. 60 s is plenty for a stable EMG mode estimate; raise idDuration if the recording's EMG character changes substantially across long sessions.
# chunkSamples
Streaming chunk size for Pass 2 (samples per channel). Default 1048576 (= 1 MiB at int16, ≈ 32 s at 32 kHz × 16 channels).
# emgClean, emgTrace, emgWaveforms
`yes`/`no` toggles for each output. Default all yes. Set emgWaveforms=no for sessions where only the timestamps are needed; set emgClean=no during initial parameter tuning to avoid rewriting the cleaned dat.
